verbs-with-prepositions.title_tr: Verbs with Prepositions (penser à, parler de, réussir à)
verbs-with-prepositions.intro_tr: In French, many verbs require a specific preposition before the noun, person, or infinitive that follows them; since this preposition almost never aligns with Turkish logic, they must be memorized individually. The two most common prepositions are "à" and "de": "penser à" (to think of/about someone or something), "parler de" (to talk about something), "réussir à" (to succeed in) are among the main examples. Some verbs, on the other hand, take no preposition and take the object directly (écouter, regarder, attendre) — Turkish speakers often mistakenly add a preposition here. Moreover, some verbs take on a completely different meaning depending on the preposition they take: if "jouer à" means to play a game/sport, "jouer de" means to play an instrument; "manquer à" and "manquer de" are also quite different from each other. On this page, the most commonly used verbs with prepositions, structures formed with infinitives, and typical error points are collected in table form.

tables.caption_tr: Main verbs used with the "à" preposition
rows: Il a réussi à son permis.
Les enfants obéissent à leurs parents.
Ils ont assisté à la réunion.

tables.caption_tr: Main verbs used with the "de" preposition
rows: Je me souviens de ce jour.
Ne te moque pas de lui.

tables.caption_tr: Verbs that take NO preposition and take the object directly (warning: common mistakes)
rows: İngilizce 'listen to' etkisiyle yanlışlıkla edat eklenebilir.
'chercher à' sadece mastarla kullanılır: chercher à comprendre.
'demander qch à qn' = birinden bir şey istemek/sormak.
İngilizce 'pay for' etkisiyle hata yapılır, Fransızcada edatsızdır.

tables.caption_tr: Verbs whose meaning changes depending on the preposition
rows: birine özlem duyulmasına yol açmak (tersine yapı!)

tables.caption_tr: Verbs used with infinitive (infinitif): à, de, or no preposition?
rows: chercher à, arriver à, réussir à, apprendre à, commencer à, continuer à, hésiter à, s'habituer à, tenir à, aider à, inviter à
décider de, essayer de, finir de, refuser de, oublier de, regretter de, choisir de, permettre de, empêcher de, arrêter de, avoir envie de, avoir peur de
Elle a arrêté de fumer. (Sigarayı bıraktı.)
vouloir, pouvoir, devoir, savoir, aimer, détester, aller, il faut
footnotes_tr: 'venir de + infinitive' (e.g. je viens de manger) is a separate structure; it expresses the near past tense and should not be confused with the preposition verb list here.

tables.caption_tr: Verbs with two complements: à + person, de + action/thing
rows: demander à qn de faire qch
Je demande à Paul de venir.
permettre à qn de faire qch
Elle permet à son fils de sortir.
conseiller à qn de faire qch
promettre à qn de faire qch
Il promet à sa mère de rentrer tôt.
La pluie nous empêche de sortir.

examples.translation_tr: We are talking about politics.

examples.translation_tr: He/She plays football, he/she plays piano.

si-clauses.intro_tr: In French, conditional sentences constructed with "si" (if) are structured according to three different tense agreement patterns, and each pattern expresses a different degree of reality: a situation that is likely to occur, a hypothetical situation that is not currently real, or a situation that never occurred in the past. The golden standard of the rule is as follows: the "si" clause NEVER uses futur simple or conditionnel — this is the most frequent mistake made by Turkish students. Whichever type is used, the tense of the subordinate clause beginning with "si" and the tense of the main clause form a fixed pair, and these pairs cannot be changed. In the tables below, the structure of three types, full conjugations, and frequently made mistakes are provided in detail.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Structure: Three Types of Conditional Sentences
rows: Gerçek / olası koşul (şimdi veya gelecekte gerçekleşebilir)
Si tu veux, je viens. / je viendrai. / viens !
Gerçek dışı koşul (şu an geçerli olmayan, hayali/varsayımsal durum)
Si j'avais de l'argent, je voyagerais.
Si j'avais su, je serais venu(e).
footnotes_tr: GOLDEN RULE: The verb immediately after 'si' can NEVER be futur simple or conditionnel. Only présent, imparfait, or plus-que-parfait can follow.
Types cannot be mixed: combining the 'si' clause of Type 1 with the result of Type 2 (e.g., *Si tu viens, je viendrais*) is incorrect.

tables.caption_tr: Complete Conjugation of the Verb "parler" in the Tenses Used in Conditional Sentences
footnotes_tr: The 'si' does not undergo elision in all cases (si + il = s'il, si + elle = si elle — it only shortens with 'il/ils').

tables.caption_tr: Participle Agreement in Verbs Conjugated with the Auxiliary être (example: aller)
footnotes_tr: In verbs conjugated with être (aller, venir, partir, arriver, rester, reflexive verbs, etc.), the participle agrees with the subject's gender and number.

tables.caption_tr: Frequently Made Mistakes (Wrong / Correct)
rows: Si tu viens, je serai content.
si + futur simple asla kullanılmaz; si + présent olmalı.
Si j'avais su, je serais venu.
si + conditionnel asla kullanılmaz; si + plus-que-parfait olmalı.
Si j'étais riche, j'achèterais une maison.
Tip 2'de sonuç cümlesi conditionnel présent olmalı, présent değil.
Si tu m'avais appelé, je serais venu(e).
Tip 3'te sonuç cümlesi conditionnel passé olmalı, conditionnel présent değil (zaman uyumsuzluğu).
*S'il vient demain...* (koşulda gelecek anlamı için futur kullanma isteği)
S'il vient demain... (présent kullanılır, anlam zaten gelecektir)
Fransızcada gelecek anlamı si-cümleciğinde présent ile verilir, ayrıca futur eklenmez.

tables.caption_tr: Other Uses of "si" Outside of Conditionals
rows: Ana cümle yok; kalıplaşmış teklif ifadesidir.
Si on gagnait, on faisait la fête.
Je ne sais pas s'il viendra.
Burada 'si' koşul bağlacı değildir; bu yüzden futur/conditionnel kullanılabilir.
Genel geçer gerçek ('quand' ile eş değer)
Si on chauffe l'eau à 100°, elle bout.
footnotes_tr: 'si' + 'il/ils' → shortens to 's'il/s'ils'; 'si' + 'elle/elles' does not shorten.

examples.target: Si tu viens demain, je serai content.

examples.target: Si tu avais étudié, tu aurais réussi l'examen.

examples.target: Si elle était venue, nous l'aurions vue.

examples.target: Si on allait au restaurant ce soir ?

double-pronouns.intro_tr: In French, when both a direct and indirect object pronoun (or y/en) need to be used in a sentence at the same time, these pronouns are not arranged randomly but according to a STRICT ordering rule. This ordering changes depending on whether the sentence is an affirmative/negative simple sentence or an affirmative imperative sentence: in simple sentences, pronouns come BEFORE the verb according to a fixed group order; in affirmative imperative sentences, they come AFTER the verb and the order nearly reverses. Patterns like 'le lui' (it to him/her), 'm'en' (it to me) are the most frequently encountered examples of this system. Memorizing this rule is one of the keys to fluent and natural French speech.

tables.caption_tr: Pronoun Group Order in Simple Sentences (Affirmative/Negative, Non-Imperative) — BEFORE the Verb
footnotes_tr: Rule: Group 1 > Group 2 > Group 3 > Group 4 > Group 5 are arranged in this order.
In the same sentence, generally at most 2 (sometimes 3) pronouns are used together.

tables.caption_tr: Frequently Used Double Pronoun Combinations (Simple Sentences)
footnotes_tr: The combined use of 'le/la' + 'en' is rare; generally 'en' by itself also covers that object (e.g., 'J'en veux' = I want some of it).

tables.caption_tr: Pronoun Order in Affirmative Imperative Mood — AFTER the Verb (Reverse Order)
rows: moi, toi, lui, nous, vous, leur
footnotes_tr: Example: Donne-le-moi! (Give it to me!) — Dis-le-lui! (Tell it to him/her!) — Donnez-m'en! (Give me some of it!) — Vas-y! (Go there! / Come on!)
Before 'en', moi/toi shortens: donne-m'en, occupe-t'en.

tables.caption_tr: Pronoun Order in Negative Imperative Mood — Returns to Simple Sentence Order
rows: Ne + Grup1 + Grup2 + Grup3 + verbe + pas
Ne + Grup1 + Grup2/3 + en + verbe + pas
footnotes_tr: In negative imperative, pronouns come BEFORE the verb again, and 'moi/toi' changes back to 'me/te'.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes and Correct Usage
rows: Düz cümlede zamirler fiilden önce gelmeli.
Emirde COD (le) her zaman COI'den (moi) önce gelir.
Olumsuz emirde de COD, COI'den önce gelir.
'en' ile birlikte genelde tek COD/COI + en kullanılır, üçlü nadir ve karmaşıktır.

negation-advanced.title_tr: Advanced Negation: ne... jamais / rien / personne / plus / aucun / ni...ni
negation-advanced.intro_tr: In French, apart from "ne... pas", there are a series of structures that express negation in more detail: ne... jamais (never/not at all), ne... plus (no longer), ne... rien (nothing), ne... personne (no one), ne... aucun(e) (no/none), ne... nulle part (nowhere) and ne... ni... ni (neither... nor). In all these structures, the sentence begins with "ne", but the second part changes to a different word instead of pas, and this determines the meaning. The most critical point is that in compound tenses like passé composé, the word order changes according to the type of negation: pas/jamais/plus/rien come immediately after the auxiliary verb, while personne/aucun/nulle part come AFTER the past participle. Also, personne and rien can be the subject of the sentence, in which case "ne" comes before the verb but pas is not used. In spoken language, "ne" is often dropped, but in written language and at B1 level, it must always be written for correct usage.

tables.caption_tr: 1. Basic Advanced Negation Structures and Their Meanings
rows: Il ne boit ni vin ni bière.
Ne şarap ne de bira içer.

tables.caption_tr: 2. Word Order in passé composé (Auxiliary Verb + Participle)
rows: Je n'ai jamais mangé de sushi.
Je ne suis allé nulle part.
Je n'ai vu ni Marc ni Paul.
Ne Marc'ı ne de Paul'u gördüm.
footnotes_tr: Rule: pas/jamais/plus/rien stay 'inside' (between the auxiliary verb and the participle), personne/aucun/nulle part stay 'outside' (after the participle).

tables.caption_tr: 3. Personne and Rien: Using as the Subject
footnotes_tr: When used as the subject, pas is NOT USED; only 'ne' with personne/rien is sufficient.

tables.caption_tr: 4. Compound (Double) Negation Structures
rows: Je ne le ferai plus jamais.
O hiçbir zaman hiçbir şey söylemez.
O hiçbir zaman kimseyi davet etmez.
footnotes_tr: The order is generally: jamais > plus > rien/personne (jamais comes before the others).

tables.caption_tr: 5. Negation with Infinitive
rows: Il a décidé de ne pas venir.
Il vaut mieux ne rien dire.
ne personne + mastar (nadir, genelde 'sans personne' tercih edilir)
Il est parti sans voir personne.
footnotes_tr: In infinitive structures, 'ne' and the negation word are generally adjacent and come BEFORE the infinitive (including those other than pas).

tables.caption_tr: 6. Common Mistakes
rows: personne kullanıldığında pas EKLENMEZ, ikisi birlikte kullanılmaz.
jamais tek başına kullanılmaz, bir nesne/tümleç gerekir; ayrıca konum kontrol edilmeli.
Özne olarak personne/rien kullanılırken pas kullanılmaz.
aucun(e) her zaman participe'ten SONRA, isimden ÖNCE gelir.
İki olumsuzluk zarfı (pas + jamais) aynı anda kullanılmaz.

passive-voice.intro_tr: Passive voice (la voix passive), is constructed in a sentence by placing the object affected by the action, not the one performing the action, in the subject position; for example, instead of "The cat eats the mouse", we say "The mouse is eaten by the cat". In French, this structure is formed with "être + participe passé (past participle)" and the participle must necessarily agree with the subject in terms of gender and number (in writing, -e, -s, -es are added). The person or thing performing the action (agent/actor) is usually expressed with the preposition "par", and in some verbs expressing feelings or continuous states, with the preposition "de". The auxiliary verb être is conjugated according to the tense of the sentence (est, a été, était, sera, serait...), thus passive voice can be constructed in any tense. In everyday speech, instead of passive voice, constructions with the subject "on" or reflexive (pronominal) verb structures are frequently preferred.

tables.caption_tr: Formation of Passive Voice: Comparison by Tenses
rows: La souris est mangée par le chat.
Le chat a mangé la souris.
La souris a été mangée par le chat.
La souris était mangée par le chat.
Le chat avait mangé la souris.
La souris avait été mangée par le chat.
La souris sera mangée par le chat.
La souris serait mangée par le chat.
...que la souris soit mangée par le chat.

tables.caption_tr: Conjugations of the Auxiliary Verb être Used in Passive Voice
footnotes_tr: The past participle (participe passé) of the main verb is added next to these conjugations: être conjugation + participle = passive voice.

tables.caption_tr: Agent Preposition: par or de?
rows: Somut, fiziksel/tek seferlik eylem bildiren fiillerde (genel kural)
La lettre a été écrite par Marie.
Duygu, düşünce veya sürekli durum bildiren fiillerde (aimer, respecter, connaître, détester, admirer)
Sonuç/durum bildiren bazı ortaçlarla (couvert de, entouré de, rempli de, orné de, accompagné de)
La table est couverte de fleurs.
La maison a été construite en 1990.
footnotes_tr: With some verbs, both prepositions may be possible; 'par' emphasizes a more concrete/active action, while 'de' emphasizes a more static state.

tables.caption_tr: Agreement of the Past Participle (Participe Passé) with the Subject
footnotes_tr: In passive voice, the participle agrees not with the actual agent, but with the (passive) subject of the sentence; this agreement applies to all conjugations formed with the verb être.

tables.caption_tr: Ways to Avoid Passive Voice (Natural French Alternatives)
rows: Konuşma dilinde en yaygın alternatif; fail belirsiz/genel olduğunda kullanılır.
Genel geçerlilik, alışkanlık bildiren durumlarda tercih edilir.
La porte a été fermée par le vent.
Fail (ajan) vurgulanmak istendiğinde edilgen çatı kullanılır.

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes
rows: La lettre est écrit par Marie.

Ortaç, dişil özneyle uyumlu olmalı (-e eklenir).

Geçmişte tamamlanmış bir eylem için être passé composé'de çekimlenmeli, hem de ortaç uyumlu olmalı.

Le film a été regardé par beaucoup de gens.
Somut/etkin eylem bildiren fiillerde 'par' kullanılır, 'de' değil.
La souris a mangé par le chat.
La souris a été mangée par le chat.
Edilgen çatıda être yardımcı fiili unutulmamalı; sadece avoir yeterli değildir.

participle-clauses.title_tr: Participial Clauses (ayant terminé, une fois parti)
participle-clauses.intro_tr: Participial clauses (propositions participiales) are shortened subordinate clauses that establish a relationship of time, cause, or manner with the main clause by using a verb in -ant (participe présent) or ayant/étant + past participle (participe passé composé) form. Because conjunctions and personal conjugation are not used, it simplifies the sentence and is particularly frequently preferred in written, literary, or formal French. "Ayant terminé" (after finishing / having finished) expresses an action completed BEFORE the main action, while "une fois parti" (once gone / after going) emphasizes the moment of completion. A participial clause's own subject can be different from the main clause's subject; in this case the subject must be placed immediately before the participle (absolute construction / proposition participiale absolue). This page summarizes four basic structures, the choice of ayant/étant, and agreement rules in tables.

tables.caption_tr: Types of Participial Clauses
rows: Voyant qu'il pleuvait, il a pris un parapluie. (Yağmur yağdığını görünce şemsiyesini aldı.)
Ayant terminé, il est parti. (Bitirdikten sonra gitti.)
Le repas fini, ils sont sortis. (Yemek bitince çıktılar.)
une fois / sitôt / aussitôt + geçmiş ortaç
une fois/sitôt + geçmiş ortaç (sıfat gibi uyumlu)
Tamamlanma anı, hemen ardından gelen eylem
Une fois arrivée, elle a appelé. (Varır varmaz aradı.)

tables.caption_tr: Participe Présent Formation (Regular and Irregular)
footnotes_tr: Only avoir, être, and savoir are irregular; all other verbs are formed by dropping -ons from the nous form and adding -ant.

tables.caption_tr: Participe Passé Composé: ayant or étant?
rows: Hareket/durum fiilleri (être ile çekilenler: DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP)
footnotes_tr: The choice of auxiliary verb is exactly the same as the rule in passé composé: être verbs take étant, others take ayant.

tables.caption_tr: étant + Past Participle and une fois + Past Participle Agreement
rows: Étant parti tôt, il a évité les embouteillages.
Étant partie tôt, elle a évité les embouteillages.
Étant partis tôt, ils ont évité les embouteillages.
Étant parties tôt, elles ont évité les embouteillages.
footnotes_tr: With étant, the past participle agrees with the subject in gender/number, just as with être in passé composé. The participle used with ayant follows the avoir rule (does not change unless the COD is placed before).

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes
rows: Participe présent'i sıfat gibi çekmek: *une femme parlante*

une fois'dan sonra mastar kullanmak: *une fois arriver*
'Une fois', 'sitôt', 'aussitôt' den sonra mastar değil, özneyle uyumlu geçmiş ortaç gelir.

indefinite-pronouns.intro_tr: Indefinite pronouns (les pronoms indéfinis) are used to make a general reference without specifying a particular person, thing, or quantity; they correspond to Turkish expressions such as "everyone", "each one", "no one", "whatever" and similar. This group includes both frequently used pronouns like chacun, personne, quelqu'un as well as more formal/literary forms like quiconque, nul, and also the n'importe qui / n'importe quoi / n'importe lequel series that carry meanings of indifference or randomness in everyday language. The vast majority of these pronouns always conjugate the verb in the 3rd person singular in a sentence (chacun a, quiconque veut, personne n'est), so when used as the subject, special attention must be paid to verb agreement. The main difficulty at B2 level is being able to distinguish the register (formal/colloquial) and usage differences between quiconque, qui que ce soit and n'importe qui that appear semantically similar. The following tables present a complete list of these pronouns, the n'importe series, special uses of chacun, and common mistakes all together.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Indefinite Pronouns

cleft-sentences.title_tr: Emphasis Structures: c'est ... qui / c'est ... que
cleft-sentences.intro_tr: In French, to emphasize a particular sentence element (subject, object, adverb, prepositional phrase), the patterns "c'est ... qui" and "c'est ... que" are used; this is called an "emphasis structure" or "cleft sentence". Similarly to the logic of "...the one who is/does... is..." in Turkish, the element to be emphasized is moved to the beginning of the sentence together with "c'est", and is followed by "qui" or "que". The rule is simple: if the emphasized element functions as the SUBJECT in the sentence, use "qui"; if it functions in a role OTHER THAN SUBJECT (object, adverb, prepositional phrase), use "que". In situations involving pronouns, tense, and negation, the structure undergoes small modifications (moi qui, c'était...qui, ce n'est pas...que, and so on). This structure is used very frequently both in everyday speech and in written language and is indispensable for natural, fluent French.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Emphasis Structure: qui or que?
rows: C'est + edat + isim + que + özne + fiil
C'est à Marie que je parle.
C'est parce qu'il pleut que je reste.

tables.caption_tr: Subject Emphasis with Personal Pronouns (emphasized pronoun + qui)

tables.caption_tr: c'est / ce sont Selection, Tense and Negation Agreement

C'est ces livres que je veux.

Ce n'est pas moi qui ai fait ça.

tables.caption_tr: Emphasizing the Complements of Prepositional Verbs (preposition + noun + que)

subjonctif-usage.intro_tr: Subjonctif (mood of desire-condition), in French is not used to express a realized fact; it is used in subordinate clauses that express a subjective attitude such as desire, necessity, emotion, doubt, possibility, or purpose. It almost always appears in a subordinate clause beginning with "que" and generally occurs when the verb/expression in the main clause and the subject in the subordinate clause are different (if the subjects are the same, the infinitive is usually preferred). While indicatif is used after expressions indicating certainty, reality, or high probability; subjonctif is mandatory after expressions indicating desire, emotion, doubt, and purpose. This page presents the main verb/expression categories that trigger the subjonctif, the complete conjugation table, its comparison with indicatif, and common mistakes all in one place.

discourse-connectors.intro_tr: Text connectors (connecteurs logiques / marqueurs de discours) are words or phrases that give the text logical flow and coherence by connecting sentences and paragraphs to each other; they are indispensable especially in written and formal French (essay, report, article). Instead of the simple "mais, donc, alors" in spoken language, more elegant and precise-meaning connectors like "néanmoins, toutefois, or, ainsi" are preferred at B2 level. Each connector has its own specific function (contrast, result, addition, explanation, exemplification), a register level, and a typical position in the sentence — mixing them both obscures the text in meaning and lowers its style. This page groups the most frequently used connectors by their functions, compares the subtle semantic differences between them, and clarifies punctuation/position rules.

register-tu-vous.title_tr: Language Registers: Informal and Formal French (tu/vous)
register-tu-vous.intro_tr: In French, there are many 'registers' (registre) to express the same idea: familier (informal/slang), courant (standard/neutral) and soutenu (formal/literary). The most visible difference between these registers is the choice of tu (you singular) and vous (you plural/formal) pronouns, but the difference is not limited to pronouns alone — vocabulary, question formation, dropping 'ne' in negation, sentence structure and even letter openings and closings vary according to the register. At B2 level, the goal is to recognize which register a text or speech is in and to produce the correct language appropriate to the situation (informal with friends, formal with a boss). Using the wrong register (for example, addressing a boss with 'tu') is considered a much more serious breach of etiquette than a grammar error.

nominalization.intro_tr: Nominalization (nominalisation), is the process of transforming a verb or adjective into a noun using specific suffixes; in French, especially in written and formal language (news texts, reports, academic writings) it is used very frequently. The three most common suffix families are -tion/-sion (generally feminine), -age (generally masculine) and -ment (generally masculine), and each is added according to different rules depending on the type of verb. Sometimes multiple nouns can be derived from the same verb and they can carry different meanings (e.g. changement/change), which is why there are also exceptions that require memorization. At B2 level, the key point of this topic is to correctly know which suffix goes with which verb and the gender of the derived noun (le/la). The tables below systematically summarize the suffix families, examples, irregular forms and meaning differences.

futur-anterieur.intro_tr: Futur antérieur (future perfect tense) expresses an action that will be completed BEFORE a specific moment in the future; the closest equivalent in Turkish is the "yapmış olacağım" construction. Its structure is simple: the auxiliary verb avoir or être is conjugated in FUTUR SIMPLE, followed by the participe passé (past participle) of the main verb. This tense is most often used after temporal conjunctions such as quand, dès que, lorsque, aussitôt que, une fois que, après que; in the subordinate clause futur antérieur is used, while in the main clause futur simple is used — since both appear as "future tense" in Turkish translation, Turkish students' most common mistake is failing to make this distinction. In verbs conjugated with être and in reflexive verbs, participe passé agrees with the subject (or COD) just as in passé composé.

agreement-advanced.title_tr: Advanced Participle Agreement: Fronted COD and Pronominal Verbs
agreement-advanced.intro_tr: In French, in compound tenses formed with the auxiliary verb avoir, the participle normally does not change; however, when a direct object (COD) comes before the verb, the participle agrees in gender and number with this COD. The fronting of the COD occurs with the pronouns le/la/les, the relative pronoun que, or structures with quel/combien de + noun. In pronominal (reflexive) verbs, although être is used, the agreement logic still depends on the COD/COI distinction: if se is a direct object, the participle agrees with the subject; if se is an indirect object (COI) and the true COD comes after the verb, the participle remains unchanged. Some verbs like se rendre compte, se parler, se nuire remain unchanged as idioms, while in the faire + infinitive construction, the participle never agrees under any circumstances. This page systematically summarizes these advanced agreement rules with tables and examples.

past-infinitive.title_tr: Past Infinitive (Infinitif Passé) — après avoir fait / après être parti
past-infinitive.intro_tr: Past infinitive (infinitif passé) is used to indicate that an action was completed before another action and is generally seen with the preposition "après" (after): "après avoir fait" (after doing), "après être parti" (after leaving). This structure consists of the infinitive form of "avoir" or "être" + past participle; which auxiliary verb is used depends on which auxiliary verb is used with that verb in passé composé. This structure can only be used when the SUBJECT of the two sentences is the same; if the subjects are different, it switches to the "après que + conditional mood" structure. Participle agreement rules are exactly the same as those in regular passé composé (agreement with the subject with être, agreement with the preceding COD with avoir). If there are object pronouns, they are placed immediately before the infinitive verb (avoir/être): "après l'avoir vu".

tables.caption_tr: General Structure: avoir/être (infinitive) + Past Participle
Main Verbs Conjugated with être (Past Infinitive Forms)
Participle Agreement (Participe Passé) Rules

conditionnel-passe.title_tr: Conditionnel Passé and Past Conditional (si + plus-que-parfait)
conditionnel-passe.intro_tr: Conditionnel passé (past conditional mood) is used to express an unrealized past action, regret, reproach, or unverified past news; it corresponds to patterns in Turkish such as "would have done, would have gone". Its structure is simple: the auxiliary verb (avoir or être) in conditionnel présent form + past participle (participe passé). The most important usage area of this mood is sentences constructed with the pattern "si + plus-que-parfait, main clause + conditionnel passé" and expressing unrealized past conditionals: "Si j'avais su, je serais venu" (If I had known, I would have come). This structure is a critical turning point at B2 level because it requires the correct sequential use of three tenses (plus-que-parfait and conditionnel passé).

tables.caption_tr: Conjugation of Auxiliary Verbs in Conditionnel Présent (Foundation of Past Conditional)
Complete Conjugation of Conditionnel Passé: parler (with avoir auxiliary verb)
Complete Conjugation of Conditionnel Passé: aller (with être auxiliary verb) — Participle Agreement
footnotes_tr: In verbs conjugated with être (aller, venir, partir, arriver, entrer, sortir, monter, descendre, naître, mourir, rester, tomber, retourner + reflexive verbs), the participe passé agrees with the subject in gender and number.

tables.caption_tr: Comparison of Three Types of Conditional Sentences (si)
rows: Si tu viens, je serai content.
Şimdiki veya gelecekteki gerçekleşmesi mümkün koşul
Si j'avais de l'argent, j'achèterais une voiture.
Si j'avais su, je serais venu.
footnotes_tr: 'si' + conditionnel are NEVER used together — this is the most common mistake.
Mixed (mixte) type is also possible: Si j'avais su (plus-que-parfait), je ne serais pas ici maintenant (conditionnel présent) — the present consequence of a past condition.

relative-advanced.title_tr: Advanced Relative Clauses: lequel + Preposition and ce qui / ce que / ce dont / ce à quoi
relative-advanced.intro_tr: Advanced relative clauses come into play when simple qui/que/dont/où pronouns are insufficient: when an antecedent requires a preposition (avec, dans, pour, sur, parmi, etc.), the "lequel" family is used, and this pronoun is conjugated according to gender/number and blends with the prepositions à and de (auquel, duquel, etc.). When the antecedent is not a specific noun but an entire clause, idea, or unknown thing, the neutral "ce qui / ce que / ce dont / ce à quoi" structures are used instead. These structures are frequently encountered in B2-level formal written French; although simplified in everyday speech, knowing their correct usage makes expression much more fluent and natural. The tables below present both "lequel" conjugation and the distinction between "ce qui/que/dont/à quoi" as a permanent reference.

tables.caption_tr: Complete Conjugation of the Lequel Pronoun and à / de Blending
footnotes_tr: With prepositions other than à and de (avec, dans, pour, sur, sans, chez, parmi, entre...), lequel is used as is without any blending: avec lequel, dans laquelle, parmi lesquels.
à laquelle and de laquelle do not blend (there is no blending in the feminine form), blending only occurs in the masculine and plural forms.

tables.caption_tr: Preposition + Relative Pronoun: Is the Antecedent a Person or an Object/Concept?
rows: l'ami à qui j'écris / le sujet auquel je pense
la femme dont je parle / le livre dont j'ai besoin
la personne avec qui je travaille / l'outil avec lequel je travaille
pour lequel, sur laquelle, dans lesquels...
le collègue pour qui je vote / la boîte dans laquelle c'est rangé
parmi lesquels / entre lesquels (kişi için de lequel formu zorunlu)
les invités, parmi lesquels se trouvait le maire
footnotes_tr: After parmi and entre, even if the antecedent is a person, the 'lequel' family must be used instead of 'qui': parmi lesquels, entre lesquelles.
In the case of de + person, 'dont' is almost always preferred in both everyday and written language; 'de qui' is more often seen in questions or in very formal/literary texts.

tables.caption_tr: ce qui / ce que / ce dont / ce à quoi — Neutral (Indefinite Antecedent) Relative Pronouns
rows: Ce qui compte, c'est ta santé. (Önemli olan sağlığın.)
Je comprends ce que tu ressens. (Hissettiğini anlıyorum.)
ce dont + özne + fiil (avoir besoin de, parler de...)
C'est ce dont je rêve. (Hayalini kurduğum şey bu.)
ce à quoi + özne + fiil (penser à, s'attendre à...)
Voilà ce à quoi je m'attendais. (Beklediğim şey buydu.)
ce sur quoi / ce pour quoi / ce avec quoi
Ce sur quoi il insiste, c'est la ponctualité.
footnotes_tr: 'quoi' here refers to something inanimate/abstract; this structure is not used when a person is involved.
These structures generally create a summarizing emphasis at the beginning of a sentence: the 'Ce qui/que/dont... , c'est...' pattern is very common.

tables.caption_tr: Definite Antecedent vs Indefinite Antecedent: Which Pronoun to Choose?
rows: Le livre qui est sur la table... / Ce qui est sur la table...
Le film que j'ai vu... / Ce que j'ai vu...
L'objet dont je parle... / Ce dont je parle...
Le sujet auquel je pense... / Ce à quoi je pense...

subjonctif-passe.intro_tr: Subjonctif passé is used after a construction that requires the subjunctive (request, emotion, doubt, certain conjunctions, etc.) to express an action completed BEFORE the verb in the main clause. It is formed with the subjonctif présent of the verb "avoir" or "être" + past participle (participe passé); in other words, it is the subjunctive mood equivalent of passé composé. In verbs conjugated with être and reflexive verbs, subject-participle agreement follows the same rules as in passé composé. This tense is also commonly used in spoken language and requires mastery of subjonctif présent knowledge at B2 level.

tables.caption_tr: Subjonctif Présent Conjugation of Auxiliary Verbs (avoir / être) — The Foundation of Subjonctif Passé
footnotes_tr: Subjonctif passé = this auxiliary verb conjugation + past participle (participe passé). Example: que j'aie mangé, que je sois parti(e).

tables.caption_tr: Complete Conjugation Example with avoir: parler (to speak) — Subjonctif Passé
Complete Conjugation Example with être: aller (to go) — Watch Out for Subject-Participle Agreement!
footnotes_tr: In verbs conjugated with être (aller, venir, partir, arriver, naître, mourir, etc. + all reflexive verbs), the participle agrees in number and gender with the subject — just like in passé composé.

tables.caption_tr: Subjonctif Présent or Subjonctif Passé? Tense Agreement Rule
rows: Yan cümledeki eylem ana cümleyle aynı anda veya ondan sonra gerçekleşiyor/gerçekleşecek
Je doute qu'il vienne. (gelmesinden şüpheliyim — henüz gelmedi)
Yan cümledeki eylem ana cümle eyleminden ÖNCE tamamlanmış
Je doute qu'il soit venu. (gelmiş olmasından şüpheliyim — geçmişte olmuş bitmiş)
footnotes_tr: Important: subjonctif passé expresses RELATIVE time, not actual time — it carries the meaning of 'completed before' relative to the verb in the main clause, and does not necessarily have to be past tense (e.g., 'Il faut qu'il ait fini avant demain' = he must have finished before tomorrow).

causative-faire.title_tr: Faire and Causative Structure (Causatif): faire faire, se faire + Infinitive
causative-faire.intro_tr: The causative structure (causatif), in French, is used to express that we are causing someone else to do an action, not doing it ourselves: the "faire + infinitive" pattern corresponds to the "-tir/-dir" causative suffix in Turkish (to have done, to cause to do). For example "réparer" (to repair) → "faire réparer" (to have repaired). In this structure, the person actually performing the action (agent/intermediary) can be added to the sentence with the prepositions "à" or "par", or may not be mentioned at all. "se faire + infinitive" is a special usage that expresses either that we are having something done for our benefit (I am having my hair cut) or that something unwillingly happened to us (my wallet was stolen). In this structure, pronoun placement and past participle agreement differ from normal verbs and have irregular rules; therefore it must be learned carefully.

tables.caption_tr: 1. Basic Patterns of Faire + Infinitive Structure

Paul'e çalıştırıyorum / Paul'ü çalıştırıyorum. (Paul, faire'in doğrudan nesnesi)

faire + geçişli mastar + COD + à + kişi

faire + geçişli mastar + COD + par + kişi (belirsizlik varsa tercih edilir)

tables.caption_tr: 2. Pronoun Placement and Past Participle Agreement

tables.caption_tr: 3. Se Faire + Infinitive: Having Something Done for Oneself and Things That Happen to One

formal-prepositional-phrases.title_tr: Formal Prepositional Phrases (à l'égard de, en dépit de, au sein de)
formal-prepositional-phrases.intro_tr: Formal prepositional phrases (locutions prépositives) are fixed expressions composed of several words instead of a single preposition and frequently used in written, administrative, academic, or journalistic French. Phrases like "à l'égard de" (toward/against), "en dépit de" (despite), and "au sein de" (within/inside) are more formal and precise equivalents of simple prepositions in everyday speech (envers, malgré, dans). Almost all of these phrases end with "de" and are followed by a noun (usually with an article); the rules for contraction with articles (de+le=du, de+les=des) also apply here. At C1 level, recognizing these structures enables understanding of formal texts and enriches written expression. The tables below group the phrases according to their meanings and provide simpler equivalents from everyday language for each.

tables.caption_tr: Formal Prepositional Phrases Expressing Opposition and Concession
rows: En dépit de ses efforts, il a échoué.
Nonobstant les objections, la loi a été votée.
Il a agi au mépris des règles de sécurité.

tables.caption_tr: Formal Prepositional Phrases Expressing Topic, Interest, and Direction
rows: Il éprouve du respect à l'égard de ses parents.
Elle se sent responsable vis-à-vis de son équipe.
Nous avons discuté au sujet du projet.
En matière d'éducation, ce pays est un modèle.
Quant à moi, je n'ai pas d'opinion.

tables.caption_tr: Formal Prepositional Phrases Expressing Location, Scope, and Framework
rows: Il travaille au sein d'une grande entreprise.
Cette réunion s'inscrit dans le cadre de la coopération.
La question est au cœur du débat.
Au-delà de ces chiffres, il faut voir la réalité humaine.
En dehors de son travail, il fait du sport.

tables.caption_tr: Formal Prepositional Phrases Expressing Reason, Means, and Basis
rows: Le vol est annulé en raison du mauvais temps.
Il a trouvé ce poste par le biais d'une amie.
Il a ouvert la porte au moyen d'une clé.
En vertu de la loi, il a été libéré.
À la lumière des faits nouveaux, l'enquête a repris.
Faute de temps, il n'a pas terminé son travail.
À défaut d'un accord, le procès continuera.

tables.caption_tr: Comparison of Everyday Language with Formal Language
rows: par le biais de / au moyen de
au sujet de / en matière de
au sein de / dans le cadre de
footnotes_tr: Formal phrases are preferred in written/administrative texts, while everyday expressions are preferred in spoken language.

tables.caption_tr: Structural Rule: de + Article Contractions

bien que / quoique + subjonctif (cümle için), en dépit de + isim
'en dépit de' bir isim alır; tam bir cümle bağlamak için 'bien que' veya 'quoique' kullanılır.

examples.translation_tr: The match took place despite the rain.
examples.note_tr: 'en dépit de' is synonymous with 'malgré' but is a more formal/written register.

examples.target: Le gouvernement a pris des mesures à l'égard des réfugiés.
examples.translation_tr: The government took measures toward/against refugees.
examples.note_tr: 'à l'égard de' is always constructed with 'de'; 'des' here is the contraction of 'de + les'.

examples.target: Cette organisation joue un rôle clé au sein de l'Union européenne.
examples.translation_tr: This organization plays a key role within the European Union.

examples.target: Le projet a été annulé en raison du manque de budget.
examples.translation_tr: The project was cancelled due to lack of budget.
examples.note_tr: 'en raison de' + 'le' = 'en raison du' (contraction rule).

examples.target: Cette formation est proposée dans le cadre du programme Erasmus.
examples.translation_tr: This training is provided within the framework of the Erasmus program.

examples.target: Faute de preuves, l'accusé a été acquitté.
examples.translation_tr: The defendant was acquitted for lack of evidence.
examples.note_tr: 'faute de' is used with nouns without articles: 'faute de temps', 'faute d'argent'.

examples.target: Quant à moi, je préfère rester chez moi ce soir.
examples.translation_tr: As for me, I prefer to stay home this evening.
examples.note_tr: 'quant à' is used when the speaker emphasizes their own opinion; it is frequently seen with stressed pronouns (quant à moi/toi/lui...).

examples.target: Par le biais de cette association, ils ont pu financer le projet.
examples.translation_tr: They were able to finance the project through this association.

modalization.title_tr: Modality and Distance: sembler, paraître and Epistemic devoir
modalization.intro_tr: In French, structures used to present information not with 100% certainty but as an impression, assumption, rumor, or logical deduction are called 'modality' (modalité épistémique); this allows the speaker to take a step back from what they are saying, i.e., to create 'distance'. While sembler and paraître express an impression based on direct observation ('it seems that...'), epistemic devoir conveys a logical inference ('...must, presumably...is') — this is completely different from devoir's deontik use meaning 'to have to'. Furthermore, conditionnel (conditional mood), especially in journalistic language, is used to convey unverified information (le ministre serait... = 'it is claimed that...'). These structures frequently appear in C1-level academic, formal, and journalistic texts; using them correctly allows you to finely adjust the degree of certainty in your expression.

tables.caption_tr: Present conjugation of the verb sembler (personal and impersonal use)
rows: Je semble hésiter, mais je suis sûr.
Elle semble contente. / kişisiz: Il semble que...
footnotes_tr: sembler, like être, is a copular/state verb; in the passé composé it is conjugated with avoir: il a semblé.
sembler is always conjugated regularly like an -er verb.

tables.caption_tr: Present conjugation of the verb paraître (irregular conjugation of the connaître type)

Il paraît malade. / kişisiz: Il paraît que...
footnotes_tr: The accent on î is mandatory in the 'il/elle paraît' form before the letter 't'.
paraître is preferred more frequently than sembler in written language and formal records.

rows: Il doit être malade. → Muhtemelen hasta.

Il devrait travailler plus. → Daha çok çalışmalı (tavsiye).

footnotes_tr: Meaning is often inferred from context; whether the verb conveys state (état) or action (action) provides a clue: with state verbs (être, avoir, sembler) epistemic reading is generally predominant.

'Il paraît que' bir cümle başlatır ve indicatif alır (duyum); 'il paraît + sıfat/mastar' ise doğrudan bir görünüşü tarif eder (Il paraît fatigué).

examples.target: Il semble fatigué aujourd'hui.
examples.translation_tr: He/She looks tired today. (direct impression, personal structure)

examples.target: Il semble qu'il ait des problèmes financiers.
examples.translation_tr: Apparently he/she has financial problems. (uncertain, distance with subjunctive)

examples.target: Il me semble que vous avez raison.
examples.translation_tr: It seems to me that you are right. (personal opinion, more certain with indicative)

examples.target: Il paraît qu'elle a démissionné.
examples.translation_tr: According to rumors, he/she resigned. (information based on hearsay, il paraît que + indicatif)

examples.target: Le suspect doit être encore en ville.
examples.translation_tr: The suspect must still be in the city. (epistemic devoir: logical deduction, not obligation)

examples.target: Il a dû oublier son rendez-vous.

examples.target: Selon la presse, le ministre serait impliqué dans ce scandale.

examples.target: On dirait qu'il va pleuvoir.

passe-simple.intro_tr: Passé simple is a tense that describes events completed in the past and happening once; however, it is almost never used in modern spoken language — passé composé has taken its place. This tense appears only in literary texts (novels, fairy tales, history books, formal narratives), newspaper articles, and formal speeches. In spoken language, forms like "je fus" or "tu parlas" are never heard; these forms are recognized in reading texts only in the 3rd singular/plural persons (il/elle, ils/elles). The aim is not to PRODUCE this tense, but to UNDERSTAND it when you see it in a text. Passé simple is the literary/formal equivalent of passé composé and is generally used together with imparfait (imparfait = background/description, passé simple = successive events).

tables.caption_tr: Conjugation of Regular Verbs in Passé Simple (3 Main Patterns)
Complete Conjugation of the Most Frequently Seen Irregular Verbs
footnotes_tr: venir and tenir (and their derivatives: devenir, revenir, obtenir, retenir, etc.) form a single exceptional group: -ins, -ins, -int, -înmes, -întes, -inrent.
aller is regular and takes the suffix of the -er group (allai, allas, alla...).

examples.target: Il naquit à Paris en 1802 et mourut en 1885.
examples.translation_tr: He was born in Paris in 1802 and died in 1885. (A typical biography sentence about Victor Hugo)
examples.note_tr: Passé simple forms of naître and mourir; very frequently seen in biographies.

examples.target: Le roi entra dans la salle et tous les courtisans se levèrent.
examples.translation_tr: The king entered the hall and all the courtiers rose to their feet.
examples.note_tr: entra (-er group) and se levèrent (-er group, reflexive verb) together.

examples.target: Elle ouvrit la porte, vit le jardin et sourit.
examples.translation_tr: He opened the door, saw the garden, and smiled.
examples.note_tr: A chain of three successive events — the classic use of passé simple.

examples.target: Quand il fut arrivé, il comprit tout.
examples.translation_tr: When he arrived, he understood everything.
examples.note_tr: 'fut arrivé' is passé antérieur (verb conjugation with 'to be/être' passé simple + participe passé); frequently seen together with passé simple.

examples.target: Ils vécurent heureux et eurent beaucoup d'enfants.
examples.translation_tr: They lived happily and had many children.
examples.note_tr: One of the classic closing sentences of fairy tales; -us group conjugation of vivre and avoir.

examples.target: Napoléon devint empereur en 1804.
examples.translation_tr: Napoleon became emperor in 1804.
examples.note_tr: devenir → devint; an example of the -ins suffix group of the venir/tenir family.

examples.target: Elle pensait à son enfance pendant que le train filait à travers la campagne.
examples.translation_tr: While the train was passing through the countryside, he was thinking of his childhood.
examples.note_tr: Here imparfait (pensait, filait) is used — description/background; not passé simple, an example for comparison purposes.

examples.target: Soudain, la porte s'ouvrit et un homme entra sans un mot.
examples.translation_tr: Suddenly the door opened and a man entered without saying a word.
examples.note_tr: Passé simple conjugation of the reflexive verb s'ouvrir: s'ouvrit.

mise-en-relief.title_tr: Fronting and Topic-Comment Structure (quant à, ce que... c'est)
mise-en-relief.intro_tr: In French, special syntactic patterns are used to particularly highlight an element of a sentence or to clearly bring out 'what is being discussed' (the topic). These structures operate according to the logic of 'topic-comment' (thème-rhème): first, the thing being discussed (the topic) is moved to the beginning of the sentence, and then what is to be said about that topic (the comment) comes. Expressions like 'Quant à', 'en ce qui concerne', 'pour ce qui est de' pull a topic to the beginning of the sentence; while the structure 'ce qui/ce que/ce dont... c'est' (semi-cleft sentence / pseudo-clivée) brings a specific element clearly to the forefront. These structures are preferred especially in written, formal, and analytical language; when making comparisons, changing topics, or strongly emphasizing an idea. In everyday speech, however, the simpler 'c'est... qui/que' cleft sentence structure is much more common.

tables.caption_tr: Topic Fronting Expressions (Topicalisation)
rows: "...e gelince" — hem yazılı hem sözlü, en yaygın ve nötr
Quant à ce problème, on en reparlera.
Bu soruna gelince, sonra tekrar konuşuruz.
"...ile ilgili olarak" — resmî, tarafsız, rapor/sunum dili
En ce qui concerne le budget, rien n'est décidé.
Bütçe konusunda henüz bir şey kararlaştırılmadı.
Pour ce qui est de + isim
"...konusuna gelince" — resmî, biraz daha yazılı üslup
Pour ce qui est des résultats, ils sont excellents.
"... söz konusu olduğunda" — çok resmî, idari/hukuki/gazetecilik metni
S'agissant de ce dossier, aucune décision n'a été prise.
Bu dosya söz konusu olduğunda henüz karar alınmadı.
Pour le prix, on verra plus tard.
En ce qui me concerne, je suis d'accord.
Beni ilgilendirdiği kadarıyla, ben aynı fikirdeyim.
footnotes_tr: A comma must always be placed after all these expressions, and then the main clause (the comment) follows.

tables.caption_tr: ce qui / ce que / ce dont / ce à quoi ... c'est Structure (Semi-Cleft Sentence / Pseudo-Clivée)
rows: Ce qui m'intéresse, c'est la musique.
Ce que + Özne + V..., c'est + odak
Ce que je préfère, c'est le silence.
"de" edatıyla kullanılan fiil (avoir besoin de, parler de...)
Ce dont + Ö + V (de)..., c'est de + odak
Ce dont j'ai besoin, c'est de repos.
"à" edatıyla kullanılan fiil (penser à, s'intéresser à...)
Ce à quoi + Ö + V (à)..., c'est à + odak
Ce à quoi je pense, c'est à mon avenir.
Ce pour quoi + Ö + V..., c'est + odak
Ce pour quoi il lutte, c'est la justice.
Là où + Ö + V..., c'est + odak
Là où je veux aller, c'est à Paris.
footnotes_tr: The focus (comment) part carries the actual information of the sentence; 'c'est' functions like a kind of 'equals' sign.
The sentence can also end with '...qui/que + verb': C'est la musique qui m'intéresse (inverted order).

Günlük ve yazılı dilde en yaygın, nötr vurgu yapısı
Cümle başında konu, sonda net odak — iki aşamalı vurgu
Ce qui compte, c'est la santé.
Yazılı, resmî, analitik/felsefi metin; güçlü ve planlı vurgu

Konuşma dilinde çoğul olsa bile "c'est" çok yaygındır
Ce qui manque, c'est les preuves. (sözlü)
"quant à"dan sonra isim veya vurgulu zamir (moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous, eux, elles) gelir
Quant à lui, il refuse. (Quant à il ✗)
"ce dont" ve "ce à quoi" kullanıldığında ilgili edat (de / à) odak kısmında tekrar edilir
Ce dont elle parle, c'est de son travail.
Konu ifadesi ile ana cümle arasına mutlaka virgül konur

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes
rows: Quant à moi, je pense que...
"quant à"dan sonra özne zamiri değil vurgulu zamir kullanılır.
En ce qui me concerne moi,...
"me" zaten "beni" anlamını taşıdığından "moi" eklemek gereksiz tekrardır.
Ce qui je veux, c'est partir.
Ce que je veux, c'est partir.
Fiilin nesnesi (COD) söz konusu olduğunda "ce que" kullanılmalı, "ce qui" özneye özeldir.
Ce dont j'ai besoin, c'est repos.
Ce dont j'ai besoin, c'est de repos.
"avoir besoin de" edatı düşürülmemeli, odak kısmında "de" tekrar edilmeli.
Ce à quoi je pense, c'est mon avenir.
Ce à quoi je pense, c'est à mon avenir.
"penser à" fiilinin "à" edatı odak kısmında da korunmalı.

examples.target: Quant à moi, je préfère rester chez moi ce soir.
examples.translation_tr: As for me, I prefer to stay home this evening.
examples.note_tr: After 'quant à', a stressed pronoun (moi) is used, never 'je'.

examples.target: En ce qui concerne les vacances, nous n'avons encore rien décidé.
examples.translation_tr: Regarding holidays, we have not yet decided anything.

examples.target: Ce qui compte le plus dans la vie, c'est la santé.
examples.translation_tr: What matters most in life is health.
examples.note_tr: 'ce qui' introduces the verb in subject function; the focus comes after 'c'est'.

examples.target: Ce que je déteste, c'est le mensonge.
examples.translation_tr: What I hate is lying.
examples.note_tr: 'ce que' is here in object function (détester quoi?).

examples.target: Ce dont elle a envie, c'est de partir en voyage.
examples.translation_tr: What he/she wants (lit. what his/her soul desires) is to travel.
examples.note_tr: The 'de' of the verb 'avoir envie de' is replaced with 'ce dont', and 'de' is repeated in the focus part.

examples.target: Pour ce qui est du contrat, il sera signé demain.
examples.translation_tr: As for the contract, it will be signed tomorrow.

examples.target: S'agissant des nouvelles mesures, le gouvernement reste prudent.
examples.translation_tr: When new measures are in question, the government continues to remain cautious.
examples.note_tr: 's'agissant de' is very formal, specific to administrative and legal texts.

examples.target: Ce à quoi je pense sans cesse, c'est à notre prochain voyage.
examples.translation_tr: What I think about constantly is our next trip.
examples.note_tr: The preposition of the verb 'penser à' is retained and repeated in the focus part: 'c'est à...'.

text-cohesion.title_tr: Text Coherence and Reference Chains (celui-ci, ce dernier)
text-cohesion.intro_tr: Text coherence (cohésion textuelle) is the totality of linguistic tools that enable the sentences in a text to be connected meaningfully to each other; in French, one of its most important components is 'reference chains' (chaînes de reprise/référence) — that is, after an entity is first mentioned by name, instead of repeatedly using the same word, referring to it by means of pronouns or synonymous expressions. The celui-ci/celui-là pair is used to distinguish between two entities mentioned in the same sentence (similar to the logic of 'the latter/the former' in English but works in REVERSE order), while the ce dernier/cette dernière structure is used only to refer back to the most recently mentioned element in an unambiguous manner and is very common in formal/journalistic language. Using these structures correctly is one of the cornerstones of academic and formal French text production at C1 level; incorrect uses lead to serious semantic ambiguity.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Types of Reference Chains
rows: Daha önce adı geçen bir unsuru geri çağırır
Henüz adı geçmemiş, metnin devamında açıklanacak unsuru işaret eder
İsmi eş anlamlı/üst kavram sözcükle tekrarlama
l'animal → le félin, la ville → la métropole
footnotes_tr: Reference chains ensure the fluidity of the text and prevent unnecessary repetition; at C1 level, diversification of these tools is expected in writing.

tables.caption_tr: celui-ci / celui-là Family — Complete Declension
footnotes_tr: Critical rule: In French, celui-ci refers to the MOST RECENTLY mentioned entity, celui-là refers to the FIRST mentioned entity — this can be the reverse of Turkish/English intuition, care must be taken.
This pair is used when one wants to establish a clear contrast between TWO entities in the same sentence or adjacent sentences.

tables.caption_tr: ce dernier / cette dernière Family — Complete Declension
rows: En son adı geçen eril tekil isim
En son adı geçen dişil tekil isim
En son adı geçen eril çoğul isim
En son adı geçen dişil çoğul isim
footnotes_tr: The ce dernier structure does not create contrast; it only repeats the nearest (most recent) antecedent, removing ambiguity — therefore 'ce dernier' does not have a 'celui-là' equivalent.

tables.caption_tr: celui-ci vs celui-là vs ce dernier — Usage Differences
rows: İki (veya daha fazla) varlık arasında karşıtlık
İkisini birbirinden ayırt etmek, biri hakkında biri hakkında farklı şey söylemek
Nötr–resmî; edebî ve akademik metinlerde sık
Tek bir varlık (en son adı geçen)
Zamir belirsizliğini önlemek (il/elle yerine), tekrarı önlemek
Resmî, gazetecilik ve idari dilde çok yaygın; günlük konuşmada nadir
Günlük dilde varsayılan seçenek; iki aday varsa belirsizlik riski taşır
Konuşma dilinde de kullanılabilir, ce dernier'den daha az resmî
footnotes_tr: When there are two subjects, using 'il' creates ambiguity (which one?); in this case, celui-ci/celui-là or ce dernier is preferred.

tables.caption_tr: Other Coherence Tools
rows: Hukuki/idari metinlerde daha önce anılan unsuru kesin biçimde tekrarlama
l'un est arrivé tôt, l'autre tard

comme indiqué ci-dessus, ce qui précède
Aynı ismi tekrar etmeden sözcüksel çeşitlilik sağlama
le chat → le félin, Paris → la capitale

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes
rows: Öğrenciler genelde İngilizce/Türkçe sezgiyle celui-ci'yi 'ilk' sanır; oysa Fransızcada tam tersidir.
Le chat a vu le chien ; il a aboyé. (belirsiz)
Le chat a vu le chien ; ce dernier a aboyé.
İki eril/dişil özne varken 'il/elle' belirsizlik yaratır; ce dernier netleştirir.

ce dernier ailesi gönderdiği ismin cinsiyet ve sayısına uyar.
Aynı ismi metinde defalarca aynen tekrarlamak
Zamir, üst kavram veya celui-ci/ce dernier ile çeşitlendirmek
Aşırı sözcüksel tekrar C1 yazımında biçemsel zayıflık sayılır.

examples.target: Jean et Paul sont arrivés en retard ; celui-ci s'est excusé, celui-là non.
examples.translation_tr: Jean and Paul arrived late; the latter one (Paul) apologized, the other (Jean) did not.
examples.note_tr: celui-ci = most recently mentioned (Paul, 'latter'), celui-là = first mentioned (Jean, 'former').

examples.target: Le président a reçu le ministre ; ce dernier a annoncé sa démission à cette occasion.
examples.translation_tr: The president received the minister; the latter one (minister) took this occasion to announce his resignation.
examples.note_tr: ce dernier always refers to the most recently mentioned noun, it does not create contrast.

examples.target: Nous avons étudié deux hypothèses : celle-ci paraît plus solide que celle-là.
examples.translation_tr: We examined two hypotheses: this latter one (second hypothesis) appears more solid than the other (first).
examples.note_tr: Feminine singular contrast: celle-ci / celle-là.

examples.target: La France et l'Allemagne ont signé l'accord ; cette dernière l'a ratifié dès le lendemain.
examples.translation_tr: France and Germany signed the agreement; the latter one (Germany) ratified it the next day.
examples.note_tr: cette dernière = subject of the verb 'ratified', the most recently mentioned feminine noun (l'Allemagne).

examples.target: Les étudiants et les professeurs se sont réunis ; ceux-ci ont écouté, ceux-là ont exposé leurs revendications.
examples.translation_tr: Students and teachers gathered together; the latter ones (teachers) listened, the others (students) voiced their demands.
examples.note_tr: Masculine plural contrast: ceux-ci / ceux-là.

examples.target: Veuillez trouver ci-joint ledit document, ainsi qu'une copie de la facture correspondante.
examples.translation_tr: You will find in the attachment the document in question and a copy of the invoice pertaining to it.
examples.note_tr: ledit/ladite: used in formal correspondence to repeatedly refer to an element previously mentioned.

examples.target: L'auteur cite deux critiques : l'une élogieuse, l'autre très sévère.
examples.translation_tr: The author conveys two critiques: one full of praise, the other very harsh.
examples.note_tr: The l'un(e)... l'autre structure also creates a binary reference chain and can be used without order restriction.

examples.target: Ce qui précède montre l'importance du sujet ; ce qui suit en détaillera les conséquences.
examples.translation_tr: What was said above demonstrates the importance of the subject; what will be explained below will elaborate on its consequences.
examples.note_tr: Text-internal reference: ce qui précède (what precedes above), ce qui suit (what follows below).

word-formation.title_tr: Word Derivation: Prefixes and Suffixes (re-, dé-, -able, -eur)
word-formation.intro_tr: In French, new words are derived by adding prefixes (préfixe) or suffixes (suffixe) to existing verb/adjective/noun roots; this is the most efficient way to rapidly expand vocabulary. The prefix re-/ré- adds the meaning "again, repeatedly," while the prefix dé-/dés- serves to "undo, reverse, negate" an action. The suffix -able/-ible derives adjectives from verbs with the meaning "can be done/-able," while -eur/-euse (and -teur/-trice) produces nouns from verbs meaning "a person or machine that does a task." These affixes follow a regular logic but contain some spelling exceptions due to pronunciation convenience and historical reasons; the tables below systematically summarize these rules and exceptions.

tables.caption_tr: Prefix re- / ré- / r- : meaning 'again, repeatedly'
rows: Ünsüzle başlayan fiillerin önüne doğrudan eklenir
Sesli harfle başlayan fiillerin önüne gelir (iki sesliyi ayırmak için)
Bazı sesli-başlangıçlı fiillerde tek 'r' ile birleşir (istisna)
Bazı fiillerde köke bağlı düzensiz kaynaşma (ezberlenmeli)
geri satın almak / tekrar aramak / rahatlatmak
footnotes_tr: Rule: consonant → re-, vowel → ré- but common verbs like racheter, ramener, rappeler, rassurer, rasseoir are irregular exceptions to the rule; these must also be memorized.
re- does not always mean 'repeat'; sometimes it only adds reinforcement or 'back' meaning: retourner (to go back), rentrer (to go back in).

tables.caption_tr: Prefix dé- / dés- : negation, reversal ('-un-, undoing')
rows: Sesli harfle başlayan kökün önüne gelir
'h' harfi ile başlayan bazı köklerde de kullanılır (h okunmaz ama yazım kuralı böyledir)
footnotes_tr: dé- does not always give direct negation; sometimes it means 'undoing an action': décoller ↔ coller (to glue).
dé-/dés- should not be confused with in-/im-/il-/ir-: dé- reverses an action (défaire = to undo what has been done), while in- directly negates an adjective (incapable = incapable).

tables.caption_tr: Suffix -able / -ible : deriving adjectives with the meaning '-able, -ible'
footnotes_tr: General rule: from -er verbs mostly -able is derived (mangeable, lavable); from -re/-oir/-ir verbs mostly -ible is derived (lisible, visible), but it is not a strict rule and requires memorization.
The negative form is made with the prefix in-/im-/il-/ir-: acceptable → inacceptable, possible → impossible, lisible → illisible, réparable → irréparable.

tables.caption_tr: Suffix -eur / -euse / -teur / -trice : deriving nouns with the meaning 'person/machine that does'
footnotes_tr: General feminine rule: -eur → -euse (chanteur/chanteuse); however, words ending in -teur mostly become -teur → -trice (traducteur/traductrice, directeur/directrice).
Some -eur words do not change or behave differently: professeur (traditionally masculine, nowadays 'professeure' is used in some places), ingénieur (in some regions 'ingénieure').
The suffix -eur derives not only person nouns but also tool/machine names: ordinateur (computer), réfrigérateur (refrigerator), aspirateur (vacuum cleaner) — these have no feminine form.

tables.caption_tr: Additional information: other common prefixes at the C1 level
footnotes_tr: The choice of in-/im-/il-/ir- assimilates according to the following phoneme: im- before b/m/p (impossible), il- before l (illisible), ir- before r (irrégulier), in- in other cases (inutile).

tables.caption_tr: Common mistakes
rows: Sesli harften önce re- değil ré- kullanılır ve aksan zorunludur.
'dürüst olmayan' için dé(s)- değil mal- öneki kullanılır.
-teur ile bitenlerde dişil biçim genelde -trice'tir, -teuse değil.
in- öneki b/m/p önünde im- olarak asimile olur.
in- öneki l önünde il- olarak asimile olur.

examples.target: Il faut refaire cet exercice depuis le début.
examples.translation_tr: This exercise needs to be redone from the beginning.

examples.target: Elle a décidé de désobéir à ses parents.
examples.translation_tr: He/She decided to disobey his/her family.

examples.target: Ce roman est écrit dans un style très lisible.
examples.translation_tr: This novel is written in a very readable style.

examples.target: Son explication est difficilement compréhensible.
examples.translation_tr: His/Her explanation is in a hard-to-understand condition.

examples.target: Le vendeur nous a très bien conseillés.
examples.translation_tr: The salesman gave us very good advice.

examples.target: La traductrice a rendu le texte avant la date limite.
examples.translation_tr: The translator delivered the text before the deadline.

examples.target: Cette tache n'est malheureusement pas lavable.
examples.translation_tr: Unfortunately, this stain is not washable.

examples.target: Il a dû réécrire toute la lettre après l'erreur.

subjonctif-imparfait.intro_tr: The subjonctif imparfait is a tense of the subjunctive mood that belongs to the past, and is now largely specific to written language and literary style. When the main clause is constructed with one of the past tenses (imparfait, passé simple, plus-que-parfait) or conditionnel, according to the classical "concordance des temps" (temporal concordance) rule, the subjonctif imparfait would be used in the subordinate clause instead of subjonctif présent. This tense is derived from the passé simple root and is particularly recognized, especially in the 3rd singular person (qu'il fût, qu'il vînt etc.), by a distinct softening mark (accent circonflexe). In modern spoken French and even in most written French, this tense has been completely abandoned, with subjonctif présent simply taking its place; today it appears only in novels, theater, official legal texts, 19th-century literature, and sometimes in very formal expressions for ironic or joking purposes. Therefore, rather than actively producing this tense, it is sufficient to learn it in order to recognize it when reading literary texts.

tables.caption_tr: Formation Rule: Derivation from Passé Simple to Subjonctif Imparfait
footnotes_tr: The other 5 persons (je, tu, nous, vous, ils) always end in a plain 's', only in the 3rd singular person is a special ending with a softening mark (^) used: -ât / -ît / -ût / -înt.

tables.caption_tr: Complete Conjugation of Regular Verbs (parler, finir, vendre)
footnotes_tr: Note: In -ir group verbs (like finir) all forms except the 3rd singular person appear identical to subjonctif présent; the only distinguishing mark is the softening mark in the 'qu'il finît' form.

tables.caption_tr: Complete Conjugation of être and avoir Verbs
footnotes_tr: 'qu'il fût' and 'qu'il eût' are the two most frequently encountered forms in literary texts; they are also used in the literary form of conditional clauses (si + subjonctif imparfait).

tables.caption_tr: 3rd Singular Person Form of Frequently Used Irregular Verbs (Most Common Form in Texts)
Classical / Literary Temporal Concordance Rule (Concordance des Temps)
rows: Je veux qu'il vienne. / Je veux qu'il soit venu.
Je voulais qu'il vînt. / Je voulais qu'il fût venu.
footnotes_tr: This rule belongs to classical written language; in modern French, even if the main clause is in the past, subjonctif présent is now generally used (Je voulais qu'il vienne).

tables.caption_tr: Comparison of Everyday Spoken Language with Literary Language
rows: Subjonctif imparfait yerine subjonctif présent kullanılır — bu bugün tamamen normdur.
19. yüzyıl ve öncesi edebiyatta, resmî anlatı metinlerinde standarttır.
qu'il fût, qu'il eût, qu'il pût, qu'il dût
Sadece 3. tekil şahıs formu, çok resmî yazılarda veya kasıtlı olarak eskicil/ironik bir üslup yaratmak için kullanılır.

examples.target: Il fallait qu'il partît avant la tombée de la nuit.
examples.translation_tr: It was necessary for him to leave before nightfall.
examples.note_tr: Because the main clause 'il fallait' (imparfait) is in the past tense, subjonctif imparfait ('partît') rather than subjonctif présent is used in the subordinate clause — classical temporal concordance rule.

examples.target: Je voulais qu'elle vînt me voir avant son départ.
examples.translation_tr: I wanted him to come to see me before leaving.
examples.note_tr: 'vînt' is the 3rd singular person form of the subjonctif imparfait of the verb venir; in modern French it has been replaced by 'vienne'.

examples.target: Bien qu'il fût tard, elle continua à lire son roman.
examples.translation_tr: Despite it being late, he continued to read his novel.
examples.note_tr: The subjonctif imparfait form of the verb être is 'fût' — it should not be confused with passé simple 'il fut'; the difference in accent changes the meaning.

examples.target: Elle craignait qu'il ne pût pas venir à la réunion.
examples.translation_tr: He was afraid that he would not be able to attend the meeting.
examples.note_tr: 'ne' here is an expletive ne (it does not carry a negative meaning); 'pût' is the subjonctif imparfait form of pouvoir.

examples.target: Il eût fallu qu'elle sût la vérité dès le début.
examples.translation_tr: He should have known the truth from the very beginning.
examples.note_tr: 'Il eût fallu' (conditionnel passé 2nd form, literary) + subjonctif imparfait 'sût' — a very formal, literary structure.

examples.target: Quoiqu'il fît froid, ils sortirent se promener dans le parc.
examples.translation_tr: Despite the cold weather, they went for a walk in the park.
examples.note_tr: The subjonctif imparfait form of the verb faire is 'fît'; in the main clause, the passé simple 'sortirent' shows the temporal concordance of literary narration.

examples.target: Le professeur souhaitait que les élèves comprissent la leçon.
examples.translation_tr: The teacher desired that the students understand the lesson.
examples.note_tr: The subjonctif imparfait conjugation of the verb comprendre is 'comprissent'; nowadays it would be replaced by 'comprennent'.

examples.target: C'était le seul homme qu'elle eût jamais aimé.
examples.translation_tr: He was the only man she had ever loved.
examples.note_tr: Use of subjunctive in literary language after an expression of superiority; 'eût aimé' is an example of subjonctif plus-que-parfait, related to the topic.

ne-expletif.title_tr: Explanatory Ne (Ne Explétif): avant qu'il ne parte
ne-expletif.intro_tr: Expletive ne (explanatory/pleonastic ne), a particle of "ne" that DOES NOT carry the meaning of real negation, used only after certain conjunctions and verbs for formal/stylistic purposes. It typically appears after verbs expressing fear, avoidance, or prevention (craindre, avoir peur, empêcher, éviter), after conjunctions like avant que, à moins que, de peur que, and in comparisons of superiority/inferiority (plus... que, moins... que) before a subjunctive or indicative verb. This "ne" alone does not make the sentence negative; the meaning is affirmative unless "pas" is added — which is why one must be careful when translating into Turkish. It is particularly common in written, formal, and literary language; in everyday spoken language it is often completely omitted. At C1 level, recognizing this nuance is important both for correctly understanding what you read and for acquiring advanced writing skills.

tables.caption_tr: Conjunctions Using Ne Explétif (Conjonctions)
rows: À moins qu'il ne pleuve, nous sortirons.
Il chuchote de peur qu'on ne l'entende.
Elle se tait de crainte qu'on ne la juge.
footnotes_tr: The verb after these conjunctions is always in the subjunctive mood; it is used together with ne explétif but ne does not create negation.

tables.caption_tr: Verbs and Expressions Using Ne Explétif
rows: Je crains qu'il ne soit malade.
Il redoute qu'on ne le critique.
Je ne nie pas qu'il n'ait raison.
Je ne doute pas qu'il ne vienne.
footnotes_tr: When the verb is used affirmatively (e.g., only 'craindre que') ne explétif is normal and common; in verbs like 'nier/douter', ne explétif appears only when the verb is in negative or question form, and it is a very formal/literary usage.

tables.caption_tr: Ne Explétif in Comparison Structures
rows: Il est plus riche qu'on ne le croit.
C'est moins compliqué qu'il n'y paraît.
La réalité est autre que je ne l'imaginais.
C'est pire que je ne le pensais.
footnotes_tr: In these structures the verb is generally in the indicative mood (indicatif), not subjunctive; ne is optional and is particularly preferred in written language.

tables.caption_tr: Comparison of Ne Explétif with Real Negation (ne...pas)
rows: J'ai peur qu'il ne vienne pas.
footnotes_tr: The distinction is usually understood from context and the presence of 'pas'; ne explétif alone never creates negation.

tables.caption_tr: Situations Where Ne Explétif is Not Used or Requires Caution
rows: ne ASLA kullanılmaz: 'sans qu'il le sache' (doğru), 'sans qu'il ne le sache' (yanlış)
ne kullanılmaz; ayrıca çoğu zaman indicatif alır, subjonctif değil
ne kullanılmaz (olumlu bekleyiş bildirir, korku/kaçınma anlamı yoktur)
ne kullanılmaz (amaç bağlaçlarıdır, korku/engelleme anlamı taşımaz)
footnotes_tr: The 'sans que' exception is frequently asked on exams: since sans already carries negation, a second ne is not added.

tables.caption_tr: Register (Register): Written and Spoken French
rows: Avant qu'il ne vienne, préparez la salle.
Avant qu'il vienne, prépare la salle.
Il est probable que la situation soit pire qu'on ne le pense.
footnotes_tr: The omission of ne explétif is not considered a grammatical error; it is merely an indicator of a more casual style.

examples.target: Partez avant qu'il ne soit trop tard.

examples.target: J'ai peur qu'elle ne vienne pas.
examples.reading: je pör kel nö vyen pa
examples.translation_tr: I am afraid of him not coming. (real negation: ne...pas)

examples.target: Il est plus fort que je ne le pensais.
examples.reading: il e plü for kö je nö lö pansɛ
examples.translation_tr: Stronger than I thought.

examples.target: Évite qu'il ne t'entende.
examples.reading: evit kil nö tantand
examples.translation_tr: Prevent him from hearing you / Avoid him hearing you.

examples.target: De peur qu'il ne se fâche, elle n'a rien dit.
examples.reading: dö pör kil nö sö faş, el na ryen di
examples.translation_tr: For fear he would get angry, he said nothing.

examples.target: Elle travaille plus qu'il ne faudrait.
examples.reading: el travay plü kil nö fodrɛ
examples.translation_tr: He works more than necessary.

examples.target: À moins qu'il ne change d'avis, nous partirons demain.
examples.reading: a mwen kil nö şanj davi, nu partiron dömen
examples.translation_tr: If he doesn't change his mind, we'll go tomorrow.

ellipsis-gapping.intro_tr: In French, ellipsis (ellipse) and gapping (gapping) are the omission of the same element (verb, subject, adjective, object, etc.) to prevent its repetition in a sentence or clause. This structure appears particularly frequently in coordinated sentences with conjunctions (et, mais, ou), in comparisons, in dialogues, and in conditional expressions ('sinon', 'si possible'), making the language more fluent and less repetitive. In written and formal speech, when a common verb is omitted, a comma usually takes its place (e.g. 'Paul aime le vin ; Marie, la bière'). Ellipsis is a critical skill at the C1 level for both reading comprehension and for fluent, natural writing/speaking style; because a student who cannot correctly reconstruct sentences with ellipsis may lose meaning. This page summarizes in table form the different types of ellipsis, punctuation rules, formulaic elliptical expressions, and common mistakes.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Types of Ellipsis
rows: Paul aime le vin, Marie aime la bière.
Paul aime le vin ; Marie, la bière.
İkinci cümlecikte tekrar eden fiil düşer, yerine genellikle virgül konur.
Il se leva et il partit.
Aynı özneyle bağlanan iki fiilde ikinci özne tekrar edilmez.
Il est plus grand que je ne suis grand.
Il est plus grand que moi.
Karşılaştırılan sıfat/isim ikinci tarafta düşürülür, zamir veya kısa yapı kalır.
Fiil ve nesne düşer, sadece vurgulu zamir + 'aussi' kalır.
Je ne l'aime pas non plus.
Olumsuz cümleye katılırken fiil öbeği tamamen düşer.
Tu peux venir si tu veux venir.
Tu peux venir si tu veux.
Tekrar eden mastar ('venir') ikinci kullanımda düşer.
Sinon, si ce n'est pas possible, on annule.
'Sinon' tek başına tüm koşul cümlesinin yerini tutabilir.
Qui a fait cela ? Paul a fait cela.
Cevapta sadece yeni bilgi (odak) verilir, geri kalan her şey düşer.

tables.caption_tr: Punctuation Rules in Verb Ellipsis
rows: Paul boit du café ; Marie, du thé.
Fiilin düştüğü yerde onun boşluğunu işaretlemek için virgül (bazen noktalı virgül) kullanılır.

Eksiltili cümlecik mutlaka önceki tam cümleye bağlı olmalı, tek başına anlam taşımaz.

— Je n'aime pas l'hiver. — Moi non plus.

Pourquoi ne serais-je pas choisi(e) moi aussi ?

Le président, en visite officielle ; le Premier ministre, resté à Paris.
Ekonomik, hızlı bilgi aktarımı için tercih edilir.
